agent-prime.mission: Telegram channel digest bot with shared channel scraping, named subscriptions, public-channel normal/deep RAG over canonical Telegram posts, timezone-aware scheduled and idempotent on-demand delivery, OpenRouter-backed summaries and isolated prompt replays, LLM-first natural-language control through authorized tools, mem0-backed semantic memory, and an environment-authenticated read-only operational dashboard.

architecture.shape: single-process app with Docker-managed PostgreSQL restart

components.component: dynamic OpenRouter free-model pool with persistent quality exclusions, DeepSeek paid emergency fallback, and health backoff
mem0 semantic memory layer persisted at .data/mem0 in Docker
read-only HTTPS admin dashboard with non-blocking LLM usage telemetry
administrator-approved public knowledge catalog with isolated local Qdrant index
isolated content-free RAG experiment control plane

high-risk-invariants.invariant: No duplicate delivery per subscription/post.
Filtered posts are recorded as skipped per subscription/post and must not reappear as pending.
No duplicate stored post per channel/post_id.
No historical posts before subscribed_at in future digests.
Summary model failure, invalid structured JSON, or empty model output must still produce a short digest for non-empty posts.
Posts with empty extracted content are recorded as skipped before LLM filtering/synthesis and must not be sent to the model.
Reply-to context must not replace the current post body in summaries or digests.
OpenRouter model refresh, persistent quality exclusions, tool probing, paid emergency fallback, and model health backoff must not block digest delivery.
Digest rendering must stay Telegram-safe HTML.
Assistant visible replies and system confirmations must render as Telegram-safe HTML, not raw Markdown; product-state confirmations must be localized and bold the subscription name.
User-editable AI filter prompts are task-only; app-owned JSON, post payload, and memory-preference instructions must stay outside user-editable text.
Channel scope is per named subscription, not global per user.
Assistant product mutations must go through user-scoped tools.
Assistant notification cron must not fire more often than every 15 minutes and valid interval schedules must render without crashing assistant tools.
Subscription-list countdown labels must use the same timezone-aware cron/legacy schedule semantics as digest due checks and hide countdowns for disabled subscriptions.
Assistant must not receive direct memory mutation tools; memory is managed by the independent mem0 layer.
Local mem0/Qdrant state must live under the host-mounted .data path, stay out of git/build context, and be accessed through a single process-local memory service.
Configured product limits must cap assistant tool executions per turn, subscriptions per user, and channels per subscription without bypassing user-scoped authorization.
Prompt replay must read only persisted posts after the subscription baseline and must never send a digest or mutate delivery, chat, or schedule state.
Digest processing logs must be recorded only for completed subscription runs, remain user/subscription scoped, and never alter post delivery state.

On-demand digests must cache the rendered result by subscription, normalized period, and effective prompts; repeats must resend that result without scraping or LLM generation and must not alter scheduled delivery or processing state. The tool-rendered digest is the only visible response for its assistant turn: the assistant must not repeat, summarize, or confirm its contents.
Admin dashboard access requires an environment-configured password hash and signed HTTPS session; dashboard reads must not mutate product state.
LLM telemetry must exclude prompt/completion content and persistence failure must never block model fallback, digest delivery, or assistant responses.

The production OpenRouter API key redacts its configured PII categories before provider forwarding and flags prompt-injection matches. These external controls do not classify political, criminal, or true-crime subject matter and must not be assumed to filter model output.
Original Post.content is the only knowledge-search source of truth and citation unit; summary/full/chunk records are retrieval representations only.
Knowledge subscription retrieval applies user ownership, channel membership, and subscribed_at to parent posts before a lexical or vector result can become a source.
Multiple vector representations of one Post collapse to one parent rank and one source slot; a summary card alone is never answer evidence.

Knowledge metadata enrichment uses the configured direct DeepSeek V4 Flash model and each import stores content-free enrichment, embedding, and total cost telemetry. Failed enrichment or vector work records a bounded retry count and error, then is retried by the four-hour knowledge job without blocking other scheduler work; exhausted failures remain available to normal lexical search. Grounded-answer generation continues to use the digest summary free-model pool with the same health backoff and DeepSeek V4 Flash emergency fallback, and knowledge Qdrant lives under .data/knowledge rather than the mem0 client or collection.

Administrator JSON knowledge imports are catalog backfills, not digest events: every imported post is recorded as skipped with reason knowledge_import_backfill for subscriptions already linked to that channel, while later scraper-discovered posts retain normal digest eligibility.

BL-21 isolated lifecycle is fail-closed: every Docker/Compose call uses only the safe root-owned local Unix socket and clone-controlled HOME/config, never caller Docker context, host, or home; db-up waits with fixed bounded inspect polling only for its exact expected PostgreSQL 16 isolated db container, including its ID/name, project/service labels, derived pgdata named volume, and only the expected read-only clone-local snapshot bind. No-argument snapshot-export serializes with a private advisory lock, creates a fresh opaque 0700 generation under the fixed clone-local generations root, writes a 0600 dump and content-free manifest there, and validates the exact generation completely before atomically replacing only the same-filesystem 0600 current-pointer file. It never moves, overwrites, or deletes the prior current generation; failures and SIGKILL before the pointer switch leave it valid, while a crash after the switch leaves the validated new generation valid. Unfinished or unselected generations are ignored and cleanup is deferred. Pointer resolution rejects symlinks, escapes, malformed IDs, unexpected files, and unsafe modes. No-argument db-restore holds a shared lock, resolves and validates only current, verifies SHA/size and fixed isolated target, then executes only fixed pg_restore arguments against db; the snapshot root is read-only in db only. Neither action calls source/production.

BL-21 quality experiments keep reports and control-plane rows content-free: raw questions, answers, prompts, post text, raw provider output, and DSNs never persist; only SHA-256 identifiers/counts, safe operator codes, declared lexical configuration, aggregate metrics, timing percentiles, and costs may be written. Every persisted experiment JSON field has a single closed-schema SQLAlchemy typed boundary that rejects nested content/credential keys and all string values for ORM/Core mapped inserts; raw untyped SQL remains outside that guarantee. A campaign owns one durable hashed-channel lock, candidate configuration is unique per campaign, and invalid state transitions are refused. Dry run and opt-in execute require the active feature branch, report-safe root, manifest-bound dataset bytes, matching clone snapshot counts, and an explicitly experiment-labelled internal clone URL; execution reads each validated manifest and dataset file once through a regular descriptor, then uses only those parsed in-memory cases and snapshot counts for database control-plane and report evidence. Dry runs create no database or report state. Execute permits only declared canonical-Post lexical candidates, resolves exactly one ready catalog channel by username, rejects vector/model/reindex paths, performs token and exact-phrase ILIKE matching as escaped literals, and runs PostgreSQL Russian FTS query-only without an index. Candidate selection uses development only before holdout evaluation; the exact-phrase short-circuit must not regress against baseline on either phase. Retrieval metrics collapse duplicate canonical parents before rank cutoffs. Reports reject non-Git roots and any workspace overlapping or containing .data/knowledge. Isolated Compose replaces inherited host mounts and exposes only clone-local experiment config/data, without knowledge storage, external networks, or database host ports, and derives its safe project and database-volume names from the canonical clone path. The initial dataset can pass quantitative gates only for human review, never automatic promotion.

BL-21 candidate execute requires one positive KnowledgeEvaluationRun ID from the isolated experiment database. The row must belong to the requested ready catalog channel, have the exact labelled dataset SHA, match the active catalog index when recorded, and include all four aggregate quality metrics; missing, mismatched, or quality-incomplete legacy rows fail before a campaign is created and never trigger a baseline rerun. Runner input requires exactly the isolated URL with the sole `experiment=bl21` marker; only after validation does one canonical helper remove that non-driver marker before SQLAlchemy engine creation, and migrations use the marker-free isolated settings URL. Campaign creation persists an immutable numeric-only baseline snapshot and SHA-256 hash. Only russian_fts and exact_short_circuit challenger labels execute; reports calculate their quality deltas against that snapshot and label latency non-comparable when historical phase percentiles are absent. Passing candidates remain passing_for_review and are never promoted automatically.

BL-21 ORM campaign and candidate states, and candidate promotion decisions, bind their lowercase enum values so they match the existing PostgreSQL enum labels from migration 0016; state-transition rules remain enum-based.

When a one-off BL-21 container lacks direct Git inspection, only the guarded host launcher may supply its canonical clone's exact feature branch and full lowercase commit revision through fixed non-secret run environment metadata. Runner preflight uses that metadata only after Git is unavailable, rejects missing, malformed, wrong-branch, or direct-Git-conflicting values, and keeps direct Git authoritative whenever present.

BL-21 vector candidate preflight permits only fixed vector/hybrid summary, full, chunk, and all-representation candidates behind --execute-vector with an isolated-db baseline ID. Each has a private .data-experiment/vector Qdrant root and collection, never touches .data/knowledge, mem0, or active points. Lexical and vector candidates use only canonical Post database IDs before RRF; every Qdrant hit must exactly match an eligible candidate-local indexed KnowledgeRepresentation by point, parent, channel, active index, representation type, and ordinal before Post.content reconstructs evidence/citations. Embedding cost uses only mandatory versioned operator_override metadata at USD 0.01 per 1,000,000 input tokens, so 750,444 tokens project USD 0.007504 per rebuild; content-free model/pricing provenance, token totals, and projected/actual totals are recorded. Unknown non-embedding metadata never authorizes paid work, optional model work is free-only, the USD 1 cap remains enforced, and no vector candidate auto-promotes an active index.

primary-flows.flow: User onboarding and settings, including an editable Telegram-safe HTML /start explanation that positions the bot as an AI service for selected public text Telegram channels, focus management, flexible filtering, scheduled digests, and one allowlisted E2E group chat path.

Subscription CRUD, global preset creation, configuration, last-24-hour digest processing-log totals, subscription-list next-digest countdown labels plus visible subscription/channel limit counters, and per-user subscription limit enforcement.
Add/remove public channels per subscription with per-subscription channel limit enforcement.
Scheduled digest delivery per due subscription.

Optional batch summary generation through an hourly refreshed free-model pool that excludes permanently disqualified models, followed by DeepSeek V4 Flash as the paid emergency fallback, with OpenRouter API-key PII redaction and prompt-injection flagging, empty-post pre-skip, structured JSON schema filter-then-synthesize cascade, editable task-only AI filter prompts with app-owned mem0 preference handling, editable summary prompts, explicit target-language/plain-field prompting, source links, split messages, and short-mode fallback that preserves normal digest grouping; assistant prompt replay and on-demand delivery reuse this pipeline over persisted posts.

On-demand digest generation for one named subscription and a natural-language period resolved in the user's timezone: the assistant paginates each selected channel to the period boundary, ingests at most 100 selected posts per channel, renders and sends the digest as the turn's only visible response, then reuses an exact cached result for matching period and effective prompts without changing scheduled delivery state.

Natural-language subscription, prompt, notification, processing-log, and on-demand-digest control through assistant tools, with Telegram typing feedback, bounded tool-capable free-model selection followed by DeepSeek V4 Flash as the paid emergency fallback, a per-turn tool execution limit while the assistant works, prompt-visible product limits, simple capability/how-to-use explanations for user questions, and prompt replay as the first response to dissatisfaction after the assistant obtains an explicit desired result, before prompt proposal or explicit prompt-application confirmation.

Authenticated read-only administrator dashboard at csd.ai-research.arha.digital with responsive 24-hour, 7-day, all-time from the first stored event, and custom UTC views of product growth, activity, delivery, LLM usage/cost since telemetry started, current channel errors, latest manually-labelled RAG retrieval metrics, and mobile-safe dd.mm chart axes.
Assistant chat history and mem0 semantic memory retrieval/extraction, with local memory stored under the Docker .data bind mount.

Administrator-approved public knowledge catalog import and four-hour bounded retry/indexing of canonical Telegram posts into fixed-schema summary/full/chunk representations, with normal, deep, or mixed grounded assistant search, original-post citations, and manually-labelled offline retrieval evaluation.

Isolated local BL-21 retrieval-quality experiment control plane: canonical config/dataset resume identities, parent-unique retrieval metrics, deterministic ID-hash train/holdout partitioning, a durable content-free campaign/candidate store with per-channel locking and strict states, stable aggregate dev/holdout records, and a manifest/database/root preflight. Dry run is write-free; explicit execute requires one validated isolated-db baseline evaluation row and persists its immutable content-free snapshot/hash, then runs only separately labelled russian_fts and exact_short_circuit challengers against one ready catalog channel. Reports include quality deltas and explicitly non-comparable historical latency when phase percentiles are absent; selection remains development-only and never promotes automatically. It never starts bot/scheduler runtime, calls providers/Qdrant, or rebuilds indexes. The isolated launcher fail-closes Compose control to static config/identity, app-only build, fixed no-deps db-up for canonical db, fixed db-only snapshot-export, fixed no-deps migration, and a fixed no-deps runner with documented isolated arguments; arbitrary services, flags, entrypoints, detached execution, and shell-shaped inputs are rejected.

BL-21 vector candidate foundation: --execute-vector with an isolated-db baseline ID validates only allowlisted vector/hybrid summary, full, chunk, and all-representation candidates, candidate-private .data-experiment Qdrant roots/collections, canonical-parent RRF, eligible-representation hit binding, and mandatory versioned operator embedding cost metadata. The gate is preflight-only until a separately authorized metered run; it does not call providers/Qdrant during implementation or promote an active index.

verification-policy.rule: Before editing, identify impacted entities, flows, invariants, and tests.
For backlog feature requests, clarify ambiguous requirements and edge cases with short one-at-a-time questions before coding; use only as many as needed, up to about 10.
For backlog feature work, shape the clarified result against the feature-spec template at .planning/backlog/_FEATURE-SPEC-TEMPLATE.md.
If behavior, invariants, or verification expectations change, update the matching knowledge-graph files in the same change.
Prefer the smallest correct code change.
Run the narrowest relevant tests first, then broader integration only if impact crosses flow boundaries.
If no true end-to-end automation exists for the impacted scenario, state the gap explicitly; if only an opt-in real Telegram path exists, say that too.

agent-usage.step: Load only the relevant neighborhood from project-graph.xml.
Load the matching scenario entries from e2e-scenarios.yaml.
Read only the implicated code files.
Report changed entities/files, impacted flows/invariants/scenarios, tests run, remaining gaps, and technical debt logged in .planning/TECH_DEBT.md if any.
